facts.statement: The genus Ruixinia contains only one known species, Ruixinia zhangi.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Ruixinia zhangi, known from a partial articulated skeleton.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen preserves the most complete series of tail vertebrae known from any Asian titanosauriform.
facts.quote: This specimen preserves the most complete series of caudal vertebrae known from any Asian titanosauriform.

facts.statement: Ruixinia had a neck over 4 meters long consisting of at least 15 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: The neck of Ruixinia was over 4 meters long and consisted of at least 15 cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: In Ruixinia, the fused tail vertebrae form a rodlike structure.
facts.quote: In Ruixinia, the fused vertebrae form a rodlike structure.

facts.statement: The chevrons of Ruixinia are distinctive, with the 20th caudal vertebra having a pentagonal shape.
facts.quote: The chevrons are distinctive, particularly that of the 20th caudal vertebra, which has a pentagonal shape.

facts.statement: The Ruixinia holotype specimen was found in the Yixian Formation in Beipiao, Liaoning Province, northeastern China.
facts.quote: The Ruixinia holotype specimen, ELDM EL-J009, was found in sediments of the Yixian Formation in Beipiao, Liaoning Province, northeastern China.

facts.statement: The locality where Ruixinia was found is dated to the Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: This locality is dated to the Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The species name honors Ruixin Zhang, a contributor to the Erlianhaote Dinosaur Museum.
facts.quote: The binomial honors Ruixin Zhang, a contributor to the Erlianhaote Dinosaur Museum.

facts.statement: Ruixinia is a member of the Jehol Biota.
facts.quote: Ruixinia is a member of the Jehol Biota.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ruixinia is a titanosaur, as some researchers suggest affinities with mamenchisaurids based on similarities with Mamenchisaurus.
facts.quote: However, both Daxiatitan and Xianshanosaurus have also been suggested to have affinities with mamenchisaurids, and Mo et al. noted several similarities between Ruixinia and Mamenchisaurus.

facts.statement: Han et al. (2024) recovered Ruixinia as a member of the Euhelopodidae, placing it as the sister taxon to Jiangshanosaurus.
facts.quote: In their 2024 description of the basal titanosaur Gandititan, Han et al. included Ruixinia in their phylogenetic analyses, recovering it as a member of the Euhelopodidae, rather than the Titanosauria, as the sister taxon to Jiangshanosaurus.

facts.statement: Averianov and colleagues (2025) proposed that Ruixinia is a non-lithostrotian titanosaur based on the anatomy of its anterior caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: In 2025, Averianov and colleagues reassessed the phylogenetic relationships of Tengrisaurus and other early titanosaurs and allied taxa. They proposed that the initial interpretation of Ruixinia as a non-lithostrotian titanosaur was supported based on the anatomy of the anterior caudal vertebrae, and since this region of the skeleton is not preserved in undisputed euhelopodids.

facts.statement: Ruixinia is classified within the unranked family Somphospondyli.
Ruixinia zhangi lived approximately 125 million years ago during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Ruixinia zhangi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Ruixinia de dinosaurio saurópodo somfospodílo que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 125 millones de años, entre el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Ruixinia is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
